markdown_content: ## Overview of Texture-Based Nesting in Clo 2025.0 This section introduces the updated nesting capabilities in Clo 2025.0, focusing on texture-based nesting, print matching, and locking patterns in place within the print layout. These features help maintain precise texture alignment from the 3D window through to the fabric nesting process, improving accuracy and production efficiency. --- ## Texture-Based Nesting: Maintaining Texture Alignment from 3D Window to Nesting Texture-based nesting in Clo 2025.0 ensures that the placement of textures and prints set up in the 3D window is preserved during the nesting process in the print layout. This feature is critical for designers, tech designers, and production teams who want to maintain exact texture positioning on garment patterns. ### How It Works - Select the pattern pieces in the 3D window that you want to nest. - In the Property Editor, under the Fabric section and below Fabric Grain Direction, locate **Pattern Matching**. - Choose **Texture Based** if your fabric’s base texture (color map) should be followed in nesting. This is ideal when working with textures that are not all-over or irregular prints. - Once selected, the system automatically locks pattern placement to prevent accidental movement. - When you use **Nest Current Fabric** in the print layout, Clo nests the patterns while preserving the texture alignment exactly as arranged in the 3D window. ### Locking Behavior - The texture lock prevents manual movement of the texture in the Edit Texture tool, though scaling remains possible. - Pattern pieces are also locked in the print layout, meaning they cannot be repositioned after nesting, ensuring consistency. - This lock enables nesting optimization for fabric consumption while maintaining texture fidelity. ### Example Use Cases - Nesting multiple graded pattern pieces with consistent texture alignment. - Visualizing how texture-aligned nesting affects fabric utilization and pricing. - Ensuring exact placement of specific texture details on garments, reducing production errors. --- ## Pattern Matching Options: Texture Based, Print Based, and Lock in Place Clo 2025.0 provides three main pattern matching options under the Property Editor for fabric nesting: ### 1. None - Default setting. - Nesting focuses solely on optimizing fabric consumption. - No attempt is made to align texture or print patterns. - Texture appearance may change during nesting as it prioritizes material efficiency. ### 2. Texture Based - Use when the fabric has a base texture or color map you want to preserve. - Ideal for fabrics without all-over or complex prints. - Locks texture position and pattern pieces to maintain visual consistency. - Supports scaling but prevents texture movement. ### 3. Print Based - Designed for fabrics with an **add print**—a design added over a plain fabric base. - Select **Print Based** when following the print overlay rather than the base fabric texture. - Useful for garments with layered prints or decals. - When selected, nesting aligns pattern pieces according to the print placement. ### 4. Lock in Place - Best for garments with fixed graphic placements, such as jeans with whiskers, washes, or other specific design elements. - Enables manual placement of pattern pieces exactly where desired in the print layout. - After placement, select **Lock in Place** to prevent movement during nesting. - Remaining patterns can be nested normally without restrictions. - Ensures critical graphic elements remain correctly positioned through production. --- ## Practical Workflow Examples ### Texture-Based Nesting Workflow 1. Arrange your garment texture in the 3D window exactly as desired. 2. Select the relevant pattern pieces. 3. In the Property Editor, select **Pattern Matching > Texture Based**. 4. Use **Nest Current Fabric** in the print layout. 5. Patterns will nest with texture alignment preserved and locked. You can repeat the nesting to optimize fabric consumption while keeping the texture consistent. ### Print-Based Nesting Workflow 1. For garments with an add print, select the pattern pieces in the 3D window. 2. Set **Pattern Matching > Print Based** in the Property Editor. 3. Nest in the print layout to align pattern pieces according to the print overlay. 4. This ensures prints added on top of the base fabric stay aligned. ### Lock in Place Workflow 1. In the print layout, manually position pattern pieces with critical graphic details (e.g., whiskers on jeans). 2. Select those pieces, right-click, then choose **Pattern Matching > Lock in Place**. 3. Other patterns can be nested normally. 4. This prevents accidental changes to important design elements during nesting. --- ## Benefits and Impact on Production - **Accurate Texture Placement:** Maintains exact texture and print placement through nesting, preventing distortions or misalignments. - **Improved Production Efficiency:** Reduces errors and rework by locking patterns in place and preserving designer intent. - **Fabric Consumption Optimization:** Allows nesting that balances fabric savings without sacrificing texture integrity. - **Enhanced Pricing Accuracy:** Enables clear visualization of fabric usage and complexity, aiding in cost estimation. - **Flexible Workflows:** Supports various fabric and print types including base textures, add prints, and fixed graphic placements. --- ## Summary Clo 2025.0 introduces advanced texture-based nesting options that allow designers and producers to maintain precise texture and print alignments from 3D garment setup through to fabric nesting. Through the use of pattern matching modes—Texture Based, Print Based, and Lock in Place—users can optimize fabric consumption while preserving critical visual elements. These features streamline production workflows, improve accuracy, and enhance communication between design and manufacturing teams.
